description: "I've added it": check whether a fix is live on the site. Use this when the owner says they have added, pasted or published a fix, or asks "is it live" or "did it work." Reads the live site for the fix request `id` (from get_fix, or a fix's newest request in list_fixes) and records what it found: `live`, or what is missing, each named. For the business-facts fix the home page's structured data has to state every fact the fix stated; for llms.txt, /llms.txt has to answer with a valid file; for the robots.txt lines, /robots.txt has to let in every assistant the fix named. A site that did not answer is not called missing the fix (`reached` false). One check a minute per request: asked again sooner it answers CHECKED_RECENTLY with retry_after. It does not predict any change in AI visibility; the weekly check observes that. Requires a Website Auditor subscription ($49/month; eligible new customers get a 7-day free trial — payment method required, no charge until the trial ends) — if the user doesn't have one, call get_sample_audit first to show them the exact output format, free and with no API key.

id.description: The fix request's id: `request.id` from the fix as served, or a fix's newest `request.id` in the site's fix list.

reached.description: False when the site did not answer, which says nothing about the fix.
